hook.line: Everyone at the café has an opinion about Altamira. *Para mí* at the front of a sentence says this is my view, which sounds softer and friendlier than stating it as fact.
hook.es: Para mí, Altamira no va a ganar.
hook.en: For me, Altamira isn't going to win.

rule:
*Para mí,* + your opinion = in my view, for me.
Ask back with *¿Y para ti?* (or *¿Y para usted?*).
Answer short: *Para mí también*, *Para mí no*.

Two small things. *Mí* here has an accent (it's me, not my); *ti* never does.

And the comma matters. *Para mí, este café es muy bueno* is your opinion. *Este café es para mí* just means the coffee is yours to drink.

options: In my view, this coffee is good.

pitfalls.why: Without the accent, *mi* means my; you need *mí*.
*Ti* never takes an accent, even though *mí* does.
